stimulus.body: Source note: A devolution of powers downward. Devolution lets local needs shape policy, but it can create uneven standards and coordination costs across regions; national goals may be harder to enforce.

questions.stem: Using the source note, explain the purpose of devolving powers downward.

questions.topic: Effective rate of protection
questions.learningObjective: Explain what the effective rate of protection measures

stimulus.body: A transit board reviews a tariff schedule. The nominal tariff on the final good is 20 percent, while imported inputs face a 10 percent tariff.

questions.stem: A source note on effective rate of protection reads: "It measures protection on value added, not just on output" Using that evidence, given those tariffs, which statement about effective protection is correct?

options.text: It equals the nominal tariff on the final good.
options.misconception: confuses nominal tariff with effective protection

options.text: It ignores tariffs on imported inputs.
options.misconception: overlooks input tariffs in value added

options.text: It measures protection on value added, not just on output.
It is always zero for exported goods.
options.misconception: reads the evidence as It is always zero for exported goods instead of It measures protection on value added, not just on output.
